butterchurn 2.6.7, the MilkDrop visualiser in WebGL 2, by Jordan Berg.
MIT licence: LICENSE, beside this file, as the package ships it.

Where these files come from

  stable release, the 3.0 line being still in beta), from
  https://registry.npmjs.org/butterchurn/-/butterchurn-2.6.7.tgz
  integrity sha512-BJiRA8L0L2+84uoG2SSfkp0kclBuN+vQKf217pK7pMlwEO2ZEg3MtO2/o+l8Qpr8Nbejg8tmL1ZHD1jmhiaaqg==
  git head d90f271be02969d8f16a3ed6b6960c971da6eff9 of github.com/jberg/butterchurn

  butterchurn.min.js  the package's lib/butterchurn.min.js, byte for byte

  LICENSE             the package's LICENSE, byte for byte
                      sha256 e5c204814d7119c939d9f111691e0c2008607d09c2f4679691e6dc5a10f24b98

  The checksums are held by tests/test_ui_visualiser.py: a changed file
  fails the suite until this note says what it is now.

What the bundle carries
  Its one bundled dependency is ecma-proposal-math-extensions 0.0.2 (Rick
  Waldron, MIT by its package.json, which ships no licence file). Loading
  the bundle defines Math.clamp, Math.scale, Math.fscale, Math.radians,
  Math.degrees, Math.DEG_PER_RAD and Math.RAD_PER_DEG, and the globals
  sqr, sqrt, sign, rand, randint, bnot, pow, div, mod, bitor, bitand,
  sigmoid, bor, band, equal, above, below, ifcond, memcpy and log10 on
  window, for MilkDrop's preset equations. None of the page's own code
  uses those names, and the bundle is loaded only when the visualiser
  first starts.
  It fetches nothing: there is no URL in it.

What is not here
  No preset pack. butterchurn-presets is labelled MIT under Jordan Berg's
  name, but its presets are other people's MilkDrop presets, converted,
  with no licence from their authors. The presets the rig shows are its
  own: ../../visualiser-presets.js.
